request.system: You recommend one pick from this draft board. The board is the world: player_id and every alternative must be a player_id on board. hint_argmax_vols is a calculator, not the answer. If you pick someone else you must set VOLS_DISSENT. If you are not the best available ECR you must set ECR_DISAGREE, and do not pick beyond ecr_best + margin. The board is capped; do not read scarcity from its length. Wait versus take is yours. Set coin_flip when a rerun of this same board could reasonably name a different player. flags is a closed set: ECR_DISAGREE, BYE_STACK, POSITION_RUN, EMPTY_STARTER, UPSIDE, VOLS_DISSENT. When you set VOLS_DISSENT, name hint_argmax_vols's player once in why as "<player> is the VOLS pick", then say why you pass. When you set ECR_DISAGREE, name ecr_best's player once as "<player> is the ECR pick", then say why you pass. Write each label one time. Do not repeat the phrase or restate the pick you passed on. The board is lean. Call detail(player_ids) once for the players you are deciding between to read delta_starter_points, the ECR spread (ecr_min/max/std), gp, points, and bye. Batch every id into that one call. Ids must be on the board.

tools.description: Heavier per-player columns for the players you are deciding between: delta_starter_points, the ECR spread (ecr_min/max/std), gp, points, bye. Batch every id into one call. Ids must be on the board.

samples.why: Superflex is empty and the two QBs on the board are the only ones who can fill it at a real premium: 35.5 delta_starter_points versus 22.5 for the best flex-capable back. qb-sf-a is also the best available ECR (44) with a tight spread (min=max=44, std 2.0), 17 gp and 191 points, so there is no conflict between value and consensus. With 11 picks until 66 and most teams between me still needing a superflex body, waiting almost certainly costs both QBs; the RB/WR/TE options here are replaceable later. Bye 10 does not collide with my roster.

SUPER_FLEX is empty and the two QBs on the board are the only ways to fill it with real starter value; qb-sf-a is both the best ECR here and the biggest starter upgrade (+35.5 over replacement, 191 pts in 17 games). With 11 picks until my next turn and most teams between still needing a SUPER_FLEX, waiting risks losing both QBs and settling for a flex body. Bye 10 is clean against my current roster.

Superflex is still empty and this is the highest-value arm on the board: 191 points, +35.5 over the starter baseline, a full 17 games, and the tightest ECR at 44 with no spread. The two QBs here are the only players who clear +34 delta; rb-f and wr-f sit around +22, so the flex/RB2 gap is much cheaper to fill later than a starting second QB. With 11 picks until 66 and several teams between me also carrying an unfilled superflex need, both quarterbacks will likely be gone. Bye 10 is clean against my held QB (8), RB (5), and WRs (7, 11).

Eleven picks until my next turn with six of the ten intervening teams still needing a superflex QB, so both QBs likely disappear before pick 66 while flex-eligible RB/WR of this tier keep replenishing. Bye 10 is clean against my held QB (8) and skill players (5/7/11).

Superflex is empty and this is the top board value by every measure: best ECR (44), highest points (191 over 17 games) and the largest starter gain (+35.5, a full 13 points clear of the best RB/WR here). Nearly every roster ahead of my next pick at 66 still needs a superflex arm, so two QBs will not survive 11 picks; taking the better one now rather than hoping qb-sf-b falls. Bye 10 does not collide with anything I hold.
